findings.fix: Remove the account number field from sign-up, or make it optional for the subset of customers who already hold one.
findings.violation: This account-creation form requires an account number before the account it is creating exists, so the task of signing up cannot use the answer: a new customer has no account number yet.

findings.violation: The form mixes 14 required and 1 optional fields and marks none of them, so the person cannot tell which may be left empty.
A control that clears everything entered sits directly beside the submit button.

findings.evidence: <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button> <button id="reset-btn" type="reset">Clear form</button>
findings.fix: Give the primary submit button a visually stronger style (filled background or more weight) than Clear form, or remove the reset control per FORMS-RESET-BUTTON.
findings.violation: Neither the primary submit button nor the reset button carries any declared styling, so the destructive secondary action renders exactly as prominently as the action that commits the form, and a person must read both labels to tell which one saves their entries.

findings.fix: Drop preferred contact time from account sign-up and ask for it when contact is arranged.
findings.violation: Preferred contact time answers a later step, a future conversation, that creating an account does not need now and could ask when contact is actually scheduled.

findings.fix: Keep one name field (or one split pair), and remove the other so the person's name is asked once.
